standard_prerequisites.name: Covering sieves characterized by sheafification
standard_prerequisites.use: Describes the covering sieves in terms of the sheafification functor.

standard_prerequisites.name: Sheafification as the left adjoint of the inclusion
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the sheafification functor is determined by the category of sheaves.

core_obligations: One direction (proof lines 11964-11965): if the two topologies are equal then their categories of sheaves are equal by definition.

Converse (proof lines 11965-11975): covering sieves are characterised by the sheafification functor, and the sheafification functor is the left adjoint of the inclusion of the category of sheaves, so if the two categories of sheaves coincide then so do the sheafification functors and hence the collections of covering sieves, whence the topologies are equal.
proof_roadmap: Use the characterisation of covering sieves by sheafification.
Use that sheafification is the left adjoint of the inclusion to conclude equality of the topologies.
difficulty_reason: The theorem states that two topologies on a category are equal if and only if they have the same sheaves (statement lines 11951-11961). The proof is a complete argument: one direction is immediate (proof lines 11964-11965); for the converse the author uses that covering sieves are characterised by the sheafification functor (proof lines 11965-11967), that the sheafification functor is the left adjoint of the inclusion of the category of sheaves (proof lines 11967-11970), so that equality of the categories of sheaves forces equality of the sheafification functors and hence of the covering sieves (proof lines 11971-11975). The non-formal content is the two-step characterisation. The claim is H1/H2: a short but complete argument with each input named.
